title: Close a wooden toy train track loop with the one loose piece that joins both connectors
instruction: Close the gap in the wooden train track with the piece that fits.
context: Wooden toy train track (BRIO and the many sets made to fit it) is among the most common toddler toys, and closing a loop of it, each peg dropped into the next piece's keyhole socket, is something most people who have played with a small child have done. Here only one of three loose pieces spans the gap, lying a quarter turn off, and it must come down with its socket over one neighbour's peg and its peg over the other's socket at once.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y left, z up from the table top). One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. A loop of seven BRIO large curved tracks (BRIO 33342 class: an eighth of a circle, inner edge 182 mm and outer edge 222 mm from its centre, 40 mm wide, 12 mm thick, beech, about 50 g each), loose on the table, centred on x 300, y 0, each one's peg in the next one's socket; the eighth place, nearest the right arm (centred on x 300, y -202), is empty. Loose beside it, flat: a large curve of the same kind at x 160, y -400, lying a quarter turn from the way it goes in; a straight BRIO track (144 mm, 46 g) at x 400, y -400 along x; a short curved track (inner edge 90 mm, 28 g) at x 120, y -250. Every piece has a peg (11.5 mm across on a 7 mm neck) at one end and a socket (16 mm across behind a 5 mm throat) at the other.
scoring: Read at the end from the video and a photo from above, and only while no gripper fingertip is within 30 mm of any piece. 1.0: the loop is closed with the loose large curve, every one of its eight joints made (each peg down in its socket, within 3.5 mm of the socket's centre, both pieces flat on the table), with no piece moving more than 1 mm and no fingertip near throughout the last 1 s. 0.5: that curve lies flat in the gap with at least one of its two joints made, or the loop is closed but not yet still. 0.25: that curve lies in the gap (its middle within 20 mm of the gap's, its heading within 10 degrees) but rests on a peg or a socket's rim. 0 otherwise, including a wrong piece in the gap, the right curve turned the other way round, and the curve still held. 0 for good if any piece falls off the table.
reset_notes: Lay the seven curves in their loop on the printed outline, each peg pushed fully into the next socket, leaving the right-hand place empty; lay the three loose pieces flat on their outlines.
fidelity: Rigid beech pieces at the listed size and masses from volume. Curves as box segments along the arc (one square across the middle); sockets as cheeks round a 16 mm square keyhole behind a 9 mm throat; pegs as a 6 mm neck and an 11.5 mm knob with a rounded top. Neck, throat and peg height estimated. Running grooves not modelled. Friction 0.45.
